text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
- Representatives of Austria's universities demand money from the government's "technology billion", saying too little research would harm the country's industry.
- Creating new jobs is Chancellor Viktor Klima's main focus at the beginning of his leadership. Austria should show more "courage to change".

- Austria's energy providers want split up the risk of market liberalisation. Provincial providers want to take over the majority in national grid company Verbund to protect themselves against foreign competition.
- Carinthia's savings bank says a consortium of Die Erste savings bank and other Austrian savings banks should take over AVZ's majority stake in GiroCredit.
- Steelmaker Boehler Uddeholm may pay out a higher dividend for 1996 as pretax profits managed to hold steady in 1996 despite difficult market conditions.
- Klima says his government does not plan any further austerity measures in the near future. However, Austria's social system will have to be restructured.
- Tourism income was up three percent in Vienna last year.
- Fibre maker Lenzing is fighting hard against losses as prices and demand remain low, restructuring is costly and the new Lyocell production plant is making losses.
- The EU commission is expected to present its decision on Bank Austria's takeover of Creditanstalt by the end of March. Bank Austria will then decide on a capital increase.
- Austria accounts for half of the European Union's bio-farmers.
- Retail turnover rose one percent in 1996.
